evals.name: crash-setup-full-path
evals.prompt: My program D:\Work\Billing\bin\Debug\net8.0\Billing.exe keeps crashing unexpectedly. Monitor it and capture a dump on the next crash. Source is at D:\Work\Billing.
evals.expected_output: Runs doctor, registers the target with the FULL --exe path and --project, keeps Full dump (does not set Mini), lists targets, and foreground-verifies with run. Does not attempt to edit/fix Billing or write its own procdump wrapper.

assertions.text: Uses CrashMonitor (not a hand-rolled procdump/try-catch)
target add uses the full EXE path D:\Work\Billing\bin\Debug\net8.0\Billing.exe, not a bare name
Does NOT set --dump Mini (Full default preserved)
Passes --project D:\Work\Billing
Runs doctor before/around setup
Foreground-verifies with run (e.g. run --seconds 60)
Does not try to modify or fix the target program

evals.name: hang-deadlock
evals.prompt: A native program becomes completely unresponsive after running for a while. I want to know where it is stuck. The exe is C:\Tools\Grabber\grabber.exe.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes hang -> deadlock path, registers the target (keeps deadlock detection ON), explains a dump is captured only after a real wait-cycle is confirmed via WCT then CDB !cs -l -o, and does not disable deadlock detection.

assertions.text: Registers grabber.exe with its full path C:\Tools\Grabber\grabber.exe
Keeps deadlock detection on (does NOT pass --deadlock false)
Explains dump only fires on a confirmed thread wait-cycle (WCT / CDB), not on a briefly-busy app
Does not claim it will fix or unstick the program

evals.name: analyze-existing-dump
evals.prompt: I have a crash dump at D:\dumps\crash.dmp. Help me determine why it crashed.
evals.expected_output: Discovers CrashMonitor and runs doctor, checks target list, uses analyze <dmp> --target when a matching target exists, and otherwise asks for the exact EXE path plus source root before registering it. It does not start live run monitoring and points the user at report.md.

assertions.text: Uses CrashMonitor analyze on D:\dumps\crash.dmp
Checks for or obtains a target ID instead of inventing one
Does not start live run monitoring
Directs the user to report.md for the result

evals.name: leak-diagnose-snapshot
evals.prompt: I have a long-running .NET service at D:\Svc\Worker\bin\Release\net8.0\Worker.exe. Its memory and handle counts keep rising over several hours. Monitor it and retain evidence when they rise. Source is at D:\Svc\Worker.
evals.expected_output: Registers the target with full path + --project, relies on the built-in diagnostics sampling (or an explicit diagnose --target --seconds --reason snapshot) rather than a crash-only run, explains a resource snapshot is a lead not proof of the leak's root cause, and does not claim to fix the leak.

assertions.text: Uses CrashMonitor (registers the target and/or uses diagnose), not a hand-rolled perfmon/procdump loop
target add uses the full EXE path D:\Svc\Worker\bin\Release\net8.0\Worker.exe with --project D:\Svc\Worker
Uses the diagnostics/diagnose path (threshold sampling or an explicit diagnose snapshot), not just a crash-only run
States a resource snapshot is a lead, not proof of the leak's root cause (deeper tooling like a heap dump is still needed)
Does not claim CrashMonitor will fix the leak

evals.name: autostart-persist-reboot
evals.prompt: I want crash monitoring to remain active on this machine after reboots. The target is D:\App\Kiosk\Kiosk.exe and the source is D:\App\Kiosk.
evals.expected_output: Registers the target with full path + --project and verifies once in the foreground, then uses scripts\Install-Autostart.ps1 for persistence, and explains it is an at-logon scheduled task (not a boot service, so it will not catch pre-login crashes) plus the elevation caveat.

assertions.text: Registers the target with the full EXE path + --project before installing autostart
Uses scripts\Install-Autostart.ps1 (not a hand-rolled service/registry Run key)
Explains autostart is login-triggered (an at-logon task), NOT a boot service and will not catch pre-login crashes
Mentions the elevation caveat (admin needed to monitor an elevated target)
Does not modify or fix the Kiosk program

evals.name: multi-instance-pid
evals.prompt: I have several instances of D:\Trade\Engine\Engine.exe. One of them is using all CPU and I want to capture evidence showing what that one is doing.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that multiple instances share one EXE path so a target/path match alone cannot pick one, identifies the hot PID, and uses diagnose --target <id> --pid <PID> to snapshot exactly that instance. Does not claim to kill or fix the process.

assertions.text: Uses CrashMonitor diagnose for an immediate snapshot (not a crash-only run)
Includes --pid <PID> to disambiguate the specific hot instance
Explains a full-path/target match alone cannot pick one instance when several share the EXE path
Does not claim to kill or fix the process
